utterances.text: Now, did the person killed have any money on him; and if so, did you keep the money?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did he have a radio station or any other radio communication device?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he only had the things you listed in your statement; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the third paragraph from the end of your statement, you said that you heard on your Motorola, on the channel used by the Serbs, that after this Serb soldier was killed, his comrades were trying to reach him on the radio, calling out, "Sumar, Sumar." That is what it says in the statement. So tell me, why would they call him over the radio if he had no radio communication device on him, as you yourself said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I wasn't with him, so I don't know where it was. He may have lost it. We didn't find it. I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. You speak of negotiations about the exchange for Filipovic, and you say the negotiations went on during the next 48 hours with Mauzer. "I talked to Mauzer over the Motorola. I claim it was Mauzer because he responded to that name when I called him on the radio to discuss the exchange."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: The man or the person who spoke to us about the exchange introduced himself as Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he introduced himself, and then you called him by that name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: He called us TO, and we called him Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he referred to you as the Territorial Defence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Referring to the documents from the bag of this killed Serb soldier, you say first, in paragraph 7: "Under those conditions, I didn't pay too much attention to those documents." Then two paragraphs later, you say about the documents that I have photocopies of here, that, "The documents are familiar to me. As I said earlier, in 1992 when I found them, I didn't pay too much attention to them, but I think that these are copies of the documents I found in Filipovic's pocket, and later on that day handed over to the intelligence officer at brigade headquarters." Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes, but I was referring to the first moment when we found the documents. However, when I was carrying these documents, these two or three documents I had occasion to look at more closely.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where did you find those documents, in a bag of a military type, as you say in paragraph 7, or in the pocket, as it says in this last quotation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Not in the -- not in his pocket but the bag, military bag, that he had on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But this is also a quotation from your statement when you said that they were copies of documents that you found in Filipovic's pocket and subsequently that day handed to the intelligence officer at brigade headquarters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: No. I claim once again that all the documents found except the ID card were documents that were in the bag. I repeat, in the military bag.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I asked you that because in one place you refer to a pocket, and in another in a bag. That's why I'm asking you about it, and now you say it's in the bag. Is that right? From what you say, it follows that you think that the documents showed to you by Ms. Pack are the same as the ones you found on the killed soldier. Does it mean that you think and that you're not quite sure? Is my understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: No. I'm quite certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. You're quite certain. And as you yourself say, in 1992 you didn't pay too much attention to those documents, and from then until the moment you had talks here, it was nine years, and now it's already 11 years, and also you were shown photocopies. Do you consider that that is a limitation on your ability to confirm that the photocopies shown to you correspond to the documents you found on the killed soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, there is some things that is imprinted in one's mind, and this is one such thing. And when I saw them again, I was quite certain they were those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the pass issued to him by the local authorities on the 7th of May, 1992, it says that Filipovic Branislav is a volunteer from Bijeljina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever learn anything about Branislav Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was he perhaps ever in the service of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And if Serbs exchanged his body for 21 Muslims, I assume he -- they cared very much about him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, if we were to establish his link with Belgrade, then things would be ideal, wouldn't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: It's not up to me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it strange, Mr. 1448, that out of the six documents that we have received, only two are dated; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Milosevic. You're trying to persuade me that I didn't find those documents, yet you are seeing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, only two of these documents have a date. You reviewed them, and surely you were able to see that for yourself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: But did you notice that they are stamped and dated?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying only two are dated. As for the others, it says in this binder that I received - gentlemen, you can see it in English - there's an indication date, unknown, then the 13th of May, and then again unknown, unknown, and then the 7th of May. So there are only two with a date. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Are you asking me anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking you: Is it clear that only two have dates on them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I really didn't review the dates, and I'd rather not go into the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. The document authorising Branislav Filipovic and Milos Blagojevic to bring ammunition to the Brcko garrison signed by Lieutenant Colonel Predrag Manojlovic from the Brcko garrison doesn't have a date. Isn't it clear that one cannot tell whether it dates back to the times prior to the secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is the when the JNA were still normally functioning in the territory of BH, or from the time when the JNA had withdrawn from Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I really don't know that, but I do know that the JNA -- I don't think it was called the JNA before that, it was just the JA.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Mr. 1448, you are wrong. The JNA was the JNA for many decades, and it was JA only very briefly after the Second World War. But never mind, that's not anything we need to prove here. It is common knowledge and can easily be verified. And then is it clear that the travel log for the Yugo doesn't say much. Although it relates to the period of March to May, it has the Brcko military post, and it says that Branislav Filipovic used the car to go to Belgrade twice. This is the period when the JNA was withdrawing from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Is this just a statement on your part?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was this the period when the army of Republika Srpska was being formed? And one cannot ascertain with certainty who owned that car and to borrow a small civilian passenger car is of no significance militarily; isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you. A car can be used for the purposes you said, but this ammunition and materiel is brought in with trucks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Then we shall focus on that. The receipt on receiving for temporary use a large quantity of ammunition and armaments on the basis of an order by the commander of the city of Belgrade I assume is the most serious document out of this set.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Well, Their Honours will decide about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Its significance is not reduced by the fact that it says: "Property received for temporary use."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes, I read that out, temporary use.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So the obligation is to return it after use. So will you tell me how you can return after use mines, hand grenades, and I don't know what else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: No. They cannot be returned, but they are used. But the weapons used to fire them have to be returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. 1448. Perhaps the significance is reduced because in the column which should have the name of the institution receiving it, it says the Territorial Defence of Brcko, which is an impossible combination now, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I really don't know which Territorial Defence you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Probably on the Serbian side, not the Bosniak side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. 1448, but what -- now, you look at it yourself. It shows that this document is a forgery, or at least that it was signed by some other Branislav Filipovic, and you didn't find it on the dead Branislav Filipovic in that in the column the name of the unit or institution which ordered the issuance of the mentioned materiel, it says by order of the KOGB, the commander of the defence for the city of Belgrade, number 3-132/2 of the 20th of June, 1992. So Mr. 1448 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, it is page 03005873 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It will be more helpful if we have the tab number --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 3. Tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [In English] "On the order of KOGB Belgrade Municipal Defence Command Headquarters -" that is within brackets - [interpretation] then the number, et cetera, of the 20th of June, 1992. Now, tell me please, Mr. 1448 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness have the document. Otherwise, he can't follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, if the soldier whose body you exchanged was killed on the 16th or 17th of May, 1992, is it possible that he should have on him a document which is a receipt that he fulfilled an order issued on the 20th of June? So a whole month after he was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you can't persuade me of something that is not true. All these documents that you have before you and which Their Honours have I found on this late gentleman. So whatever you're trying to do to persuade me of something that is not true, I really -- I apologise, but that just can't be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. 1448, are you saying that you exchanged this killed person on the 16th or 17th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does it say quite clearly here that this is on the order of the 20th of June of 1992? Are these facts --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You made the point. You made the point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. May. As you have limited my cross-examination to the documents, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in tab 3, I have a photocopy of this receipt, and I see that the witness has in his hands the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: On the receipt that I have, one cannot see this date in the top right-hand corner, 13th of May, 1992. And also, one can't see the date in June. Can you see it on your copy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes, both dates can be seen very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: And you believe that the date written in the top right-hand corner and the date in connection with this order, that they correspond?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I don't think anything; all I can say is what I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Could you now explain to Their Honours the document found on this Serb soldier killed behind the front line where you were; is that right? On the other side where units of this other army were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: You said here in the third paragraph: "We pulled out the body from the place where he was killed and headed to our side of the line near to the coffee bar called Elvis."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you had to cross to the other side of the front line.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: We are not understanding one another. Behind the line means the rear, in the rear of our own line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just explain to the Judges what was the reason for you to expose yourself to the danger of bullets to pull out a dead Serb soldier's body?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: The reason is simple: At the beginning we didn't know whether he was a Serbian soldier or our soldier because it was between houses and a factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: Was he in a uniform or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Sir, I have to explain. Where this happened there are houses and bushes, and when we came close up, we saw that he was a Serbian soldier in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So you thought at first that he may be one of your men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I do have a few questions in re-examination. Can the witness be handed, please, tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, you've been handed an original of the documents, copies of which you were shown when you wrote your statement. Witness, look, please, at the date at the top of the document in handwriting. Is it handwritten on the top of the document the 13th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall anything about the condition of the documents that you found in the bag on the dead soldier?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: When you found the documents on the dead soldier, were they clean documents, in a good condition, or what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: They were not quite clean.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Tell us what condition they were in.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Well, the time has its effect, but roughly like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, is this one of the documents that stood out in your mind when you retrieved documents from the bag?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Chamber, please, why that was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: I'll try to be brief. When I moved from the front line to the brigade headquarters, I saw figures of these assignments. Compared to what we had in those days, this was rather big, and that is why it was -- it stuck in my mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: By "assignments," are you talking about the equipment that we see listed on the receipt?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the part of this document, the authorisation, which describes the types of ammunition that Branislav Filipovic has permission to carry from Belgrade to Brcko, ammunition for 30-millimetre and 20-millimetre anti-aircraft guns.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to assist us, and please say if you aren't, as to how the ammunition identified here corresponds to the ammunition described in the receipt that you were looking at earlier at tab 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-1448
utterances.text: Because on that occasion in that battle, we captured a 30-millimetre anti-aircraft gun, a three-barrelled one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Ms. Pack, we have to leave, so if you have any more questions, could you deal with them fairly rapidly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an observation to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, quickly, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very quickly. There is no anti-aircraft three-barrelled, 30-millimetre gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You can present some evidence about that in due course.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only 20-millimetre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Witness B-1448, thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give your evidence. It's now over, so you're free to go. Would you just wait, though, please, for the blinds to be drawn before you do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 30th day of October, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
